text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) approved co-fiancing of investment programmes in Poland worth 234 million zlotys in 1996. In the first five years of its activity EBRD invested 934 million Ecus in 49 projects in Poland.

- Poland's food prices in the last ten days of March inched up by 0.2 percent compared with the previous ten days and by 0.5 percent compared with the same period the month before, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.

- More than 1,100 firms from 22 countries are exhibiting their products at the Infosystem and Multimedia computer software and hardware exhibitions and the Poligrafia publishing technologies fair in Poznan, western Poland.

- TKF Poland, controlled by Denmark's Thorkild Kristensen Group, Foras Holding A/S and the Danish Investment Fund in Central and Eastern Europe, will invest $100 million in construction of two trading centres in Warsaw to accomodate France's Carrefour supermarkets and shopping and restaurant malls. The first centre will be completed by the end of this year and the other in summer 1998, TKF Poland said.

- The balance sheet total of the International Bank of Poland (IBP) was 520 million zlotys in 1996 showing a 29 percent growth compared with 1995, but the bank's net profit fell by five million zlotys to 13 million zlotys. The decline resulted from the end of IBP's tax holidays, IBP's board deputy president Janusz Czarzasty said.
- The Bank Inicjatyw Spoleczno Ekonomicznych (BISE) and the Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) banks are in talks with World Bank on a credit to finance local governments' infrastructural projects.

- The listed Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS) plans to create a financial group including a bank with a nationwide outlet system, a brokerage and an insurance company, the bank said. BOS is considering buying one of the following banks in 1997: Agrobank, Pierwszy Bank Komercyjny and Bank Podlaski.

- The finance ministry grants operation licences only to those foreign insurance companies which invest in the ailing local insurance firms, because the sector is underfunded, the ministry's insurance department director Jerzy Adamski said. About 60 insurance companies will operate in Poland by the end of 1998.
- The Pekao SA bank will not be privatised in 1997, the finance ministry said. The bank's shares will be listed on the Warsaw bourse in the first quarter of 1998 at the earliest.
- Ampli SA, an electrical engineering equipment wholesale trader in Tarnow, southeastern Poland, has applied for a share listing on the Warsaw bourse, the company said.
- The listed Ariel footwear maker's sales will reach 24.8 million zlotys earning this year and its net profit 2.6 million zlotys, Ariel's president Jozef Jedrzejczyk said.
